levels.strict: must read current data: sync only (no decision site)
levels.stale-ok: sync, copy (replicationLagSeconds 1 s) or cache (cacheTtlSeconds 60 s), each priced by O4
levels.immutable: stale-ok with zero staleness (p = 0 in O4)

rules.S1: read-modify-write: the same execution writes the data based on what it read (lost update if stale)
rules.S2: invariant guard not re-checked by a constraint, trigger or compare-and-set in the write
rules.S3: state transition decided by the read state, written without compare-and-set
rules.S4: authorization/ownership (here only together with I1: the owner column never changes, so the check is immutable)
rules.S5: same transaction / lock: the read is under a lock or must see the transaction's own writes
rules.S6: read-your-writes: the caller's own write moments earlier decides the result, which is frozen into a durable record
rules.E1: an effect call (registration with an external provider), not a read: never cache/copy
rules.R1: reference data, rarely written: a stale value is at most a slightly outdated snapshot
rules.R2: re-validated later or atomically in the write (saga step, unique constraint, trigger, compare-and-set)
rules.R3: served from an event-fed copy today and accepted by MiSArch
rules.I1: monotone data: insert-only rows / write-once or never-changing columns read by key; a stale read can only miss a row created a moment ago
